Texture orientation - faces from the texture scan review

These faces had their texture turned or mirrored so it did not run on from the faces next to it.
Each was found by ALTLevelScan, rendered before and after, and kept after review (Edward, 2026).

A turn rotates the face's four vertex indices (16 bytes at the face's offset), so the face keeps
its winding. A mirror swaps the flag byte (offset + 0x12) for its mirrored partner: 0 and 2,
4 and 6, 12 and 34, 8 and 10, 26 and 28, 30 and 32. The texture index and light bytes are
unchanged.

Face	Offset		Scan	Change	Was					Now
100	0x15E2C	381-1	three quarter-turns	7351, 8834, 7453, 7449	->	7449, 7351, 8834, 7453


==== The see-through floors over the lift shafts (texture fix, all versions) ====

The room's 22 see-through floors each have 16 faces: an oval in the middle eight on one side, edges and corner
triangles round them. The floors are numbered by rows of the minimap, top to bottom, then left to right; in the
game, "left" is high x and "top" is low z.

1.0.0: by the minimap's columns (cells 54, 59, 64, 72, 77, 82) the ovals run left, left, right, left, right, right
(Edward, 2026). Floors 6, 11, 15, 17, 18, 20 and 22 (cells 77/22, 77/27, 64/32, 77/32, 82/32, 64/37, 77/37) were the
other way round and are mirrored left to right whole: each face takes the texture (or animator) and corners of the
face opposite it. Quads keep their winding and take the mirrored twin of their routine (12 <-> 34, 30 <-> 32);
triangles have their corners reversed, which the original draws as well, since routine 13 (0x224e8) never tests a
face's facing (it projects with 0x48924, as routine 5 does).

1.0.1 (Edward, 2026, judged from in-game renders):
- On every floor the two middle edge squares of the top row swap places and turn half way round, and so do the two
  of the bottom row.
- Floor 14 (cells 59/32) is the model. Its four corner triangles take the tile and corner order Edward chose:
  textures 294, 300, 292 and 300. The two using 300 are the closest any tile and order came; one seam of each
  still does not quite meet.
- Every other floor's corner triangles and middle edge squares are made the same as floor 14's: moved across, or
  mirrored on the 11 floors whose oval is on the other side from floor 14's (1, 4, 6, 9, 11, 12, 15, 17, 18, 20,
  22). This also gives floor 22's two left triangles a tile from the floors' own page (they used texture 0).

219 faces, one byte patch (see below). "Was" is the shipped file; "Now" is after the patch.

==== ALTENGINE ONLY - NOT FOR THE ORIGINAL GAME (stage 5, ALTEngine/data/EngineFilePatches.json, "modelFaces") ====

The lift platform (model L000, used by all 13 of the level's 4 x 4 lifts). Its two corner triangles at the
high-X/high-Z and low-X/low-Z corners, faces 1 and 14, show tile 297 cut the wrong way, so the vein from each of the
four eyes stops at them. Each becomes the mirror image of its neighbour across the lift: face 7 onto face 1 and
face 8 onto face 14 (Edward, 2026).

Why ALTEngine only: a mirrored triangle needs its corners reversed, which turns it to face down. The original's
lift loader (FUN_00041a20) only ever gives a lift face draw routine 0, 1 or 2, and all three hide a face seen from
behind, so in the original these two corners would be gaps. ALTEngine marks the faces (their +0x13 byte, which the
original never reads from the file: its loader writes the routine number there) and draws a marked door or lift face
from both sides. ALTViewer's patch button does not make this edit, and the original game should never be given it.

The edit names the face by section and number, not by offset, so it holds with the Level Cleanup on or off. It is
made after the Level Cleanup and the texture blanking, and taken out again at the start of every install run.

Face	Section	Was (20-byte record)				Now
1	L000	07000000 04000000 03000000 03000000 2901 02 00	->	04000000 07000000 03000000 03000000 2901 02 05
14	L000	13000000 02000000 14000000 14000000 2901 02 00	->	02000000 13000000 14000000 14000000 2901 02 05

Corners (7, 4, 3, 3) -> (4, 7, 3, 3) and (19, 2, 20, 20) -> (2, 19, 20, 20); texture 297 and flag 2 unchanged.
In the shipped file (after the duplicate model removals) the records are at 0x7D10C and 0x7D210; the install finds
them by section, since the Level Cleanup moves them.

==== Every patch to this file, in bytes (made from ALTEngine/data/Patches.json) ====
Offsets are into the file after the duplicate model and object removals (Patch/DUPLICATE-MODELS.txt), as the install applies them.
Each line: offset: shipped bytes -> patched bytes. To undo a patch, write the shipped bytes back.

Patch 40: L381LEV.MAP - texture orientation: 1 face(s) from the texture scan review turned or mirrored to run on from their neighbours (see Patch/L381LEV.txt) (Claude, 2026)
  0x15E2C: B7 1C 00 00 82 22 00 00 1D 1D 00 00 19 1D 00 00 -> 19 1D 00 00 B7 1C 00 00 82 22 00 00 1D 1D 00 00

Patch 68: L381LEV.MAP - the see-through floor over the lifts (Edward, 2026), first of its kind put right: faces 3283 and 3099 (3284 and 3100 in a cleaned install) turned half way round, (c, d, a, b); faces 2850 and 2860 (2851, 2861) texture 301 -> 294 and 294 -> 301
  0x256D8: A8 28 00 00 A7 28 00 00 AA 28 00 00 AB 28 00 00 -> AA 28 00 00 AB 28 00 00 A8 28 00 00 A7 28 00 00
  0x24878: A7 28 00 00 A6 28 00 00 68 28 00 00 AA 28 00 00 -> 68 28 00 00 AA 28 00 00 A7 28 00 00 A6 28 00 00
  0x23514: 2D 01 -> 26 01
  0x235DC: 26 01 -> 2D 01

Patch 75: L381LEV.MAP - the 22 see-through floors over the lift shafts put into one pattern (Edward, 2026). Each floor's middle eight faces form an oval on one side; by the minimap's columns (cells 54, 59, 64, 72, 77, 82) the ovals run left, left, right, left, right, right. Floors 6, 11, 15, 17, 18, 20 and 22 (the sheet's numbering; cells 77/22, 77/27, 64/32, 77/32, 82/32, 64/37, 77/37) were the other way round and are mirrored left to right whole: every face takes the mirror image of the face opposite it (its texture or animator, and its corners), quads keeping their winding with the routine's mirrored twin (12/34, 30/32), triangles reversed (routine 13 has no back-face test in the original, 0x224e8 projects with 0x48924 as routine 5 does). Then, on every floor, the two middle edge squares of the top row swap places and turn half way round, and so do the bottom row's (version 1.0.1). Floor 14 (cells 59/32) is the model for the rest: its four corner triangles take the tile and corner order Edward chose (textures 294, 300, 292, 300), and every other floor's corner triangles and middle edge squares are made the same as floor 14's, moved across or, on the 11 floors mirrored to it, mirrored. 219 faces; the floors' faces and offsets are listed in Patch/L381LEV.txt.
